m:sanmarco: The square is free. For the basilica you need shoulders and knees covered and no large backpacks (there's a left-luggage office nearby). Entry about €3 with a time slot booked on basilicasanmarco.it; the Pala d'Oro and the Treasury have a separate ticket. Usually open Monday–Saturday from 9:30am to 5pm, Sundays and holidays only from the afternoon (hours to be confirmed). The Campanile costs about €10 (not checked).
m:palazzoducale: Combined ticket for the St Mark's Square Museums (Doge's Palace, Museo Correr, Archaeological Museum and Biblioteca Marciana) about €30 on palazzoducale.visitmuve.it, valid for several days. Usually open every day 9am–7pm from April to October, 9am–6pm from November to March (last entry an hour before); closed on 25 December and 1 January. Hours and price to be confirmed.
m:rialto: Crossing the bridge is free. The fruit and vegetable market is open Monday to Saturday in the morning; the fish market (in the Gothic building) Tuesday to Saturday in the morning, closed on Mondays and Sundays (to be confirmed). The bridge is packed: watch out for pickpockets.
m:accademia: Ticket about €15, best with a time slot booked on gallerieaccademia.gov.it. Usual hours: Tuesday–Sunday 8:15am–7:15pm, Monday 8:15am–2pm (to be confirmed). Entry numbers are limited.
m:salute: Free entry to the church (shoulders and knees covered), usually open from 9:30am to noon and from 3 to 5:30pm, with a break at midday (to be confirmed). The sacristy has a separate ticket. On 21 November there's the feast of the Madonna della Salute, with a bridge of boats across the Grand Canal.
m:peggy: Ticket about €16, best online on guggenheim-venice.it. Open from 10am to 6pm, closed on Tuesdays and 25 December (to be confirmed). No photos in some rooms.
m:frari: Ticket about €5 (to be confirmed). Open Monday–Saturday 9am–6pm, Sunday from 1pm (hours to be confirmed). Nearby is the Scuola Grande di San Rocco, with Tintoretto's great cycles, paid.
m:ghetto: The square and alleys are free to wander. The Jewish Museum and guided tours of the synagogues are paid and closed on Saturdays and Jewish holidays. In Cannaregio the Fondamenta degli Ormesini and Fondamenta della Misericordia are full of bacari.
m:castello: Free. Until 22 November 2026 the Art Biennale is on at the Giardini and the Arsenale (separate ticket, usually closed on Mondays: check on labiennale.org).
m:zattere: Free. The squero (gondola yard) can be seen from the fondamenta opposite (you can't go in). At sunset it's a good place to sit and watch the boats.
m:isole: Take the vaporetto from the Fondamente Nove (line 12 for Murano, Burano and Torcello; Burano is about 40 minutes away, to be confirmed). The access fee isn't charged for the smaller islands. Some Murano glass workshops close in the afternoon.
vd:domori: Venice's oldest bacaro (since 1462), a short walk from Rialto: a counter of cicchetti (meatballs, salt cod, tramezzini) and wine by the glass. Eaten standing, quietly, with copper pots hanging overhead. Closed on Sundays.
vp:domori: A cicchetto costs about €2–3, an ombra (small glass) of wine about €2–3: with four cicchetti and a glass it's around €12–15 (from guides, menu not seen).
vd:allarco: A small bacaro near the Rialto market: cicchetti with fresh fish, crostini and sandwiches, served to people who work at the market. Open in the morning and at lunch, closed on Sundays.
vp:allarco: A cicchetto €2–4; a lunch of six pieces and an ombra around €15 (from guides, menu not seen).
vd:madonna: A historic trattoria near Rialto, big and noisy, with Venetian cooking: sarde in saor, spaghetti with clams, fried fish. Closed on Wednesdays.
vp:madonna: A pasta course costs about €14–18; a full meal around €30–35 (from guides, menu not seen).
vd:tonolo: The Venetians' neighbourhood pâtisserie, open since 1886 near the Frari: brioche, krapfen, fritole and traditional sweets. Closed on Mondays.
vp:tonolo: Breakfast with cappuccino and brioche around €4–5 (from guides, menu not seen).
vd:squero: A small bacaro opposite the Squero di San Trovaso: get cicchetti and an ombra and eat on the fondamenta watching the gondola builders at work.
vp:squero: Cicchetti around €2–3 each, wine by the glass around €2–4 (from guides, menu not seen).
vd:ildoge: An artisan gelateria on Dorsoduro's liveliest campo, popular with students: seasonal flavours, fruit and pistachio, to eat on the benches in the square.
vp:ildoge: A cone or a cup costs about €2.50–4 (from guides, menu not seen).
vd:timon: A Cannaregio bacaro on the canal: order cicchetti, plates of cured meats and wine by the glass and eat sitting on the moored boat or on the fondamenta. Open in the evening too.
vp:timon: A cicchetto €2–3, a board about €12–15: a light dinner is around €15–20 (from guides, menu not seen).
vd:dalmas: A pâtisserie a short walk from the station: brioche, cakes and pastries, coffee at the counter. Handy for a quick breakfast on arrival or before the train.
vp:dalmas: Breakfast around €4–6 (from guides, menu not seen).
vd:rivetta: A simple, popular trattoria two minutes from San Marco, frequented by Venetians too: pasta, fried fish and dishes of the day at fairer prices than the centre. Closed on Mondays.
vp:rivetta: A pasta course €10–14; a meal around €25–30 (from guides, menu not seen).
vd:rosasalva: A historic Venetian pâtisserie (since 1879) opposite the basilica of Santi Giovanni e Paolo: brioche, krapfen, traditional sweets and ice cream, to take away too.
vp:rosasalva: Breakfast around €5–7 (from guides, menu not seen).
vd:palmisano: A Burano bakery-pâtisserie selling bussolà, the island's ring-shaped biscuits, and baked sweets to eat while strolling among the coloured houses.
vp:palmisano: A bag of biscuits around €5–8 (from guides, menu not seen).
cd:campanile: The lift to the top of the bell tower: views over the lagoon and the rooftops.
cd:rezzonico: A palace on the Grand Canal with furnishings, Tiepolo frescoes and Venetian 18th-century art.
cn:cadoro: Franchetti Gallery at the Ca' d'Oro
cd:cadoro: A Gothic façade on the Grand Canal and, inside, works by Mantegna and Titian.
cd:sanrocco: Tintoretto's cycle of paintings, room after room.
cn:dogana: Punta della Dogana and Palazzo Grassi
cd:dogana: Contemporary art from the Pinault collection, in a former customs house on the Grand Canal.
cd:orologio: The guided tour of the clock's mechanisms and the terrace overlooking the square.
cd:sangiorgio: From the bell tower of an island opposite San Marco: the finest view of the city.
cd:fenice: The opera house rebuilt after the fire, with gilded boxes.
cd:canpesaro: Modern art by Klimt and Kandinsky in a Baroque palace on the Grand Canal.
cd:murano: Five centuries of blown glass, on the island where it's still made.
cx:murano: It's on Murano: add the vaporetto time.
